cache must be shared across threads.

"""
LRU-TTL Cache Implementation

This module provides a thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with
expiration (TTL) support. It includes a low-level cache implementation
and a high-level wrapper that exposes a clean API for end users.
A comprehensive pytest suite is included to validate correctness,
thread-safety, TTL behavior, and edge cases.

Design Overview
---------------
The cache is built on top of Python's built-in ``collections.OrderedDict``
which naturally maintains insertion order. Two auxiliary structures are
used to achieve O(1) operations:

* ``_dirty`` : an ``OrderedDict`` that stores every key currently held
  by the cache.
* ``_ttl``   : a ``dict`` keyed by cache entry that records the absolute
  expiry timestamp (``datetime.datetime`` with timezone ``UTC``).
* ``_lock``  : a ``threading.Lock`` to serialize access across threads.

When a key is set, the entry is moved to the "most recently used" position
in ``_dirty`` by using ``pop`` + ``insert``. When a key is accessed,
the same move is performed. When the cache is evicted, the oldest
(entry at the front of ``_dirty``) is removed if it has expired or if
the capacity is exceeded.

The high-level wrapper ``ThreadSafeLRUCache`` adds convenience methods
such as ``get_with_fallback`` and ``invalidate`` while inheriting the
thread-safe and TTL semantics from the core ``LRUCache`` class.

All public methods are documented with NumPy-style docstrings to make
the API discoverable and to serve as a reference for the tests.
